Maya (Docs): FYI linkcheck failed on the publish after the prune pass. saw duplicate fragment ids in quickstart. :(

Maya (Docs): snippet: 
```
Warning: duplicate fragment id detected for /guides/quickstart.html#install
Slugs generated: quickstart-install, quickstart_install
```

Maya (Docs): background: our anchor-prune job strips explicit ids from MDX files; the fallback slugifier (node-slugify@1.x) produces a different form than the builder's slugify in Docusaurus v2.1.0 when headings include em-dashes or smart quotes. yields collisions.
Eli (DevEx): repro locally with `yarn docs:check-links` (this runs the linkcheck). `npx docusaurus build` shows the final slugs the site will use.
Sasha (Platform): builder image currently uses docusaurus@2.1.0. upstream changed slugify behavior in 2.2. we should either align versions or make prune preserve explicit ids.
Maya (Docs): short-term options: 1) add explicit ids to affected headings (e.g. `## Install {#install}`), 2) change prune to keep explicit ids, or 3) add a linkcheck sanity that compares prune slugs vs build slugs.
Jon (Eng-Docs): I'll put up a hotpatch with explicit ids for the quickstart and a tiny CI gate to fail on duplicate fragments. easier and low-risk.
Maya (Docs): also spotted a docs example with an unescaped triple-backtick inside a fenced snippet which broke MDX in previews. e.g. a code sample that itself demonstrates backticks.
Eli (DevEx): we should add a lint rule in the docs linter to flag fenced examples that contain unescaped fence markers. quick fix: wrap that sample in a markdown code fence with language `md` and embed inner code as escaped HTML or use a <pre><code> block.
Jon (Eng-Docs): creating PR now: https://git.internal.redwood/p/docs/slug-collision-hotpatch/pull/7. will: add explicit ids to three headings, add linkcheck duplicate-fragment step, and a one-line note in the docs changelog.
